# NavigationShell

Header: `winui/ui/navigation/NavigationShell.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/navigation/NavigationShell.hpp`.

A navigation view: a pane of navigation items (left, compact, minimal or a top bar) beside a content area that shows the selected item's page.

Items are [NavEntry](#struct-naventry) values. The selection is reported as keys: an item's [NavEntry::key](#struct-naventry), else its text, and "settings" for the Settings item. The positional calls ([set_expanded()](#set_expanded), [text_at()](#text_at), [item_bounds()](#item_bounds)) take a pre-order index over the menu items, then the footer items, with Settings for the Settings item. A selected item shows its own [`content`](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#content), or the view's content from [set_content()](#set_content) when it has none. In Auto mode the pane adapts to the control's width. It opens and closes on its toggle button, and closes on a click outside when it overlays the content. It can host an [AutoSuggestBox](auto-suggest-box.md#uiautosuggestbox), a pane header, custom content and a footer, all owned by the view. The items are one tab stop with a keyboard cursor. The declarative form is [ui::NavigationShell](#uinavigationshell) with [ui::NavItem](#uinavitem).

Example: 
```cpp
auto nav = std::make_unique<ui::NavigationShellControl>();
nav->set_pane_display_mode(ui::NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode::Left);
nav->set_pane_title("My app");
nav->add_item("Home", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Welcome home"));
nav->add_item("Library", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Your library"));
nav->on_selection_changed([](const std::string& key) {
    if (key == ui::NavigationShellControl::SettingsKey)
        std::println("open the settings page");
});
ui::NavigationShellControl* view = window.set_content(std::move(nav));
view->set_header(view->selected_key()); // "Home": the first item is selected, keyed by its text

// Or declaratively, with one shared content region driven by the selection:
ui::Property<std::string> page;
window.set_content(ui::NavigationShell{
    .selected_key      = page, // "home" at first, then whatever the user picks
    .pane_display_mode = ui::NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode::Top,
    .content           = ui::Text{.text = page},
    .items             = {ui::NavItem{.text = "Home", .key = "home", .icon = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Home)},
                          ui::NavItem{.text = "Mail", .key = "mail", .icon = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Mail)}},
});
```

## `ui::NavigationShell`

A pane of navigation items over swappable content. Builds a [ui::NavigationShellControl](#uinavigationshellcontrol).

The selection is a key: an item's `.key`, else its text, and "settings" for the Settings item. Auto display mode picks Expanded, Compact or Minimal from the view's width against the two thresholds.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::string> page{"mail"};

window.set_content(ui::NavigationShell{
    .selected_key         = page, // two-way: a click writes the new key
    .pane_display_mode    = ui::NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode::Left,
    .on_selection_changed = [&](const std::string& key) {
        if (key == ui::NavigationShellControl::SettingsKey)
            open_settings();
    },
    .items                = {
        ui::NavItem{ .text = "Home", .key = "home", .icon = ui::IconGlyph{0xE80F}, .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Welcome" } },
        ui::NavItem{ .text = "Mail", .key = "mail", .icon = ui::IconGlyph{0xE715}, .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Inbox" } },
    },
    .footer_items = { ui::NavItem{ .text = "Account", .key = "account", .icon = ui::glyphs::Contact } },
});
```

## `ui::NavItem`

One navigation entry: the text in the pane, the content shown while it is selected, and any nested items it groups. A non-empty [`children`](#uinavitem-children) makes the row a collapsible group with a chevron.

[`.content`](#uinavitem-content) may be left unset. The view's own [`ui::NavigationShell::content`](#uinavigationshell-content) is then shown for this item.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::NavItem{ .text              = "Basic input",
             .key               = "input",
             .expanded          = true,
             .selects_on_invoke = false,
             .icon              = ui::IconGlyph{0xE73A},
             .children          = {
                 ui::NavItem{ .text = "Button", .key = "button", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "Button page" } },
                 ui::NavItem{ .text = "CheckBox", .key = "checkbox", .content = ui::Text{ .text = "CheckBox page" } },
             } }
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::NavItem{
    .text, .key, .expanded, .selects_on_invoke, .icon, .kind, .tool_tip, .animated_icon,
    .content, .info_badge, .children
}
```

| <span id="uinavitem-key"></span>`key` | `std::string` |  | What identifies the item in `.selected_key` and the selection events. Empty uses the text. "settings" is taken by the Settings item. |

## `ui::NavList`

A built, owned list of navigation entries, the braced-list form of the move-only [ui::NavEntry](#struct-naventry). Callers never name it, since a braced list of [`ui::NavItem{...}`](#uinavitem) converts to it.

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp

    .entries
}
```

## `ui::NavigationShellControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ValueProvider`.

A navigation view: a pane of navigation items (left, compact, minimal or a top bar) beside a content area that shows the selected item's page.

Items are [NavEntry](#struct-naventry) values. The selection is reported as keys: an item's [NavEntry::key](#struct-naventry), else its text, and "settings" for the Settings item. The positional calls ([set_expanded()](#set_expanded), [text_at()](#text_at), [item_bounds()](#item_bounds)) take a pre-order index over the menu items, then the footer items, with Settings for the Settings item. A selected item shows its own [`content`](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#content), or the view's content from [set_content()](#set_content) when it has none. In Auto mode the pane adapts to the control's width. It opens and closes on its toggle button, and closes on a click outside when it overlays the content. It can host an [AutoSuggestBox](auto-suggest-box.md#uiautosuggestbox), a pane header, custom content and a footer, all owned by the view. The items are one tab stop with a keyboard cursor. The declarative form is [ui::NavigationShell](#uinavigationshell) with [ui::NavItem](#uinavitem).

Example: 
```cpp
auto nav = std::make_unique<ui::NavigationShellControl>();
nav->set_pane_display_mode(ui::NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode::Left);
nav->set_pane_title("My app");
nav->add_item("Home", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Welcome home"));
nav->add_item("Library", std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Your library"));
nav->on_selection_changed([](const std::string& key) {
    if (key == ui::NavigationShellControl::SettingsKey)
        std::println("open the settings page");
});
ui::NavigationShellControl* view = window.set_content(std::move(nav));
view->set_header(view->selected_key()); // "Home": the first item is selected, keyed by its text

// Or declaratively, with one shared content region driven by the selection:
ui::Property<std::string> page;
window.set_content(ui::NavigationShell{
    .selected_key      = page, // "home" at first, then whatever the user picks
    .pane_display_mode = ui::NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode::Top,
    .content           = ui::Text{.text = page},
    .items             = {ui::NavItem{.text = "Home", .key = "home", .icon = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Home)},
                          ui::NavItem{.text = "Mail", .key = "mail", .icon = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Mail)}},
});
```

The Settings item's index in the positional calls ([text_at()](#text_at), [item_bounds()](#item_bounds), [set_selected_index()](#set_selected_index)).

```cpp
static std::string_view SettingsKey = "settings"
```

The Settings item's key, as [selected_key()](#selected_key) reports it and [set_selected_key()](#set_selected_key) takes it.

```cpp
NavigationShellControl()
```

An empty view in Auto mode with an open pane, the Settings item visible and the back button shown but disabled; it creates its own back, toggle, close and search buttons.

### set_items

```cpp
void set_items(std::vector<NavEntry> items)
```

Replaces the menu items and resets the selection to the first selectable item. A selected Settings item stays selected. The keyboard cursor and the selection indicator's animation reset too.

### set_footer_items

```cpp
void set_footer_items(std::vector<NavEntry> items)
```

Items at the bottom of the pane (the right of the top bar), above the Settings item, in the same selection model. Their indices follow every menu item's. Keeps the selection when it was a menu item or Settings.

### add_item

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* add_item(std::string text, std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

Appends a leaf at the top level of the menu items, taking ownership of its content, and returns a non-owning observer to the content. The first item added becomes selected. Use [set_items()](#set_items) for nested items.

### set_content

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_content(std::unique_ptr<T> content)
```

The content region used by any selected item whose own [`content`](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#content) is null, usually a [NavigationFrame](navigation-frame.md#uinavigationframe). Takes ownership and hands back a non-owning observer.

### item_count

```cpp
std::size_t item_count() const
```

Every item in the tree, menu and footer, collapsed ones included. This is the pre-order index space of [selected_index()](#selected_index) and [set_expanded()](#set_expanded).

### footer_item_count

```cpp
std::size_t footer_item_count() const
```

How many of those are footer items (the last ones).

### visible_row_count

```cpp
std::size_t visible_row_count() const
```

How many menu rows are currently drawn in the pane, i.e. not hidden inside a collapsed ancestor. Footer rows are not counted.

### text_at

```cpp
const std::string& text_at(std::size_t index) const
```

The text of the item at pre-order `index` ("Settings" for Settings), or an empty string if out of range.

### set_text

```cpp
void set_text(std::size_t index, std::string text)
```

Changes the text of the item at pre-order `index`; updates the layout and redraws. An item without a [NavEntry::key](#struct-naventry) is keyed by its text, so its key changes too. Out of range, and Settings, are no-ops.

### key_at

```cpp
const std::string& key_at(std::size_t index) const
```

The key of the item at pre-order `index`: its [NavEntry::key](#struct-naventry), else its text; "settings" for Settings; empty out of range.

### index_of

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> index_of(std::string_view key) const
```

The pre-order index of the first item with `key`, Settings for "settings"; unset when no item has it.

### info_badge_at

```cpp
InfoBadgeControl* info_badge_at(std::size_t index) const
```

The badge of the item at pre-order `index`, or null.

### set_info_badge

```cpp
InfoBadgeControl* set_info_badge(std::size_t index, std::unique_ptr<InfoBadgeControl> badge)
```

Replaces (or with null, removes) the badge of the item at pre-order `index`, and returns the new one as an observer. Out of range is a no-op returning null.

### set_selects_on_invoke

```cpp
void set_selects_on_invoke(std::size_t index, bool selects)
```

Changes [NavEntry::selects_on_invoke](#struct-naventry) of the item at pre-order `index`. Out of range is a no-op.

### item_at_row

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> item_at_row(std::size_t row) const
```

The item drawn at menu row `row` (pre-order index); unset if out of range.

### selected_key

```cpp
const std::string& selected_key() const
```

The selected item's key ("settings" for Settings), or empty when nothing is selected.

### set_selected_key

```cpp
void set_selected_key(std::string_view key)
```

Selects the first item with `key`; "settings" selects the Settings item and an empty key clears the selection. A key no item has is a no-op, otherwise as [set_selected_index()](#set_selected_index).

### selected_index

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> selected_index() const
```

The selected item's pre-order index, or Settings; unset when nothing is selected.

### set_selected_index

```cpp
void set_selected_index(std::optional<std::size_t> index)
```

Selects the item at pre-order `index`, clamped to the item list. Settings selects the Settings item and unset clears the selection. Does nothing, and fires nothing, if the item is already selected, is a heading (`selects_on_invoke == false`), a header or a separator, or is Settings while it is hidden. Either way the left pane scrolls the item into view on the next layout, after laying out any expansion made just before.

### settings_selected

```cpp
bool settings_selected() const
```

Whether the Settings item is the selection.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(const std::string&)> handler)
```

Fired with the new key whenever the selection changes (a click, the keyboard, [set_selected_key()](#set_selected_key), [set_selected_index()](#set_selected_index)); empty when it was cleared. A call that lands on the already-selected item does not fire it.

### on_item_invoked


## struct NavEntry

One navigation entry: the text in the pane, the content shown while it is selected, and any nested items it groups. It is plain data, not an [Element](../tree/element.md), but it owns its [`content`](#struct-naventry) subtree.

That makes it move-only, so a [`std::vector<NavEntry>`](#struct-naventry) is built by pushing into it. For a braced list use [`ui::NavItem`](#uinavitem)/[`ui::NavList`](#uinavlist) from this header.

Example: 
```cpp
auto                      nav = std::make_unique<ui::NavigationShellControl>();
std::vector<ui::NavEntry> items;

ui::NavEntry home{"Home"};
home.icon    = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Home);
home.content = std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Welcome");
items.push_back(std::move(home));

ui::NavEntry mail{"Mail"};
mail.icon       = ui::symbol_glyph(ui::Symbol::Mail);
mail.expanded   = true;
mail.info_badge = std::make_unique<ui::InfoBadgeControl>();
mail.children.push_back(ui::NavEntry{"Inbox"});
mail.children.push_back(ui::NavEntry{"Sent"});
items.push_back(std::move(mail));

nav->set_items(std::move(items)); // pre-order indices: Home 0, Mail 1, Inbox 2, Sent 3
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | The row's text; a header's title. Also the tooltip and the automation value when the item is selected. |
| `content` | `std::unique_ptr<Element>` |  | The content shown while this item is selected. May be null, and then the view's own content ([NavigationShellControl::set_content](#set_content)) is shown instead. That is usually a [NavigationFrame](navigation-frame.md#uinavigationframe) when the items carry no pages at all. |
| `children` | `std::vector<NavEntry>` |  | Nested items. A non-empty list makes this row a collapsible group with a chevron. |
| `expanded` | `bool` | `false` | Whether a group shows its children inline in the left pane. False by default. |
| `selects_on_invoke` | `bool` | `true` | Whether invoking the row selects it. False makes the row a pure heading: it still expands and collapses, but never becomes the selection. |
| `icon` | `IconSource` |  | The icon, drawn at 16 DIPs in the row's icon column: a [Symbol](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#symbol), a glyph, a path or a picture. |
| `info_badge` | `std::unique_ptr<InfoBadgeControl>` |  | A badge drawn between the text and the chevron. |
| `kind` | `NavEntryKind` | `NavEntryKind::Item` | An item, a section header or a separator. A header shows [`text`](#struct-naventry) and a separator nothing; neither is ever selected, invoked or given the keyboard cursor. |
| `tool_tip` | `std::string` |  | The row's tooltip. Empty shows the text, and only while the pane is closed compact. A non-empty one shows in every mode. |
| `animated_icon` | `std::unique_ptr<AnimatedIconControl>` |  | An animated icon, drawn instead of [`icon`](#struct-naventry) in the pane's rows and the top bar in the row's text color. Its state follows the row's: PointerOver while hovered, Pressed while pressed, Normal otherwise. [`icon`](#struct-naventry) still names the row's icon everywhere else (the overflow and children flyouts), so set it to the animated icon's fallback glyph. |
| `key` | `std::string` |  | What identifies the item in selected_key() and the selection events. Empty uses [`text`](#struct-naventry). "settings" is taken by the Settings item. |

## struct NavigationShellExpandedChangedArgs

What [NavigationShellControl::on_expanded_changed()](#on_expanded_changed) gets: the group whose expansion changed, and whether it is expanded now.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The group's pre-order index. |
| `expanded` | `bool` | `false` | True when it opened. |

## Enumerations

### NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode

```cpp
enum class NavigationShellPaneDisplayMode
```

Where a [NavigationShell](#uinavigationshell) puts its items.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Auto` | Expanded from expanded_mode_threshold_width() on, Minimal below compact_mode_threshold_width(), Compact between. |
| `Left` | Always Expanded: an inline pane, a compact strip while closed. |
| `Top` | The items in a 48-DIP bar across the top; what does not fit goes behind "More". |
| `LeftCompact` | Always Compact: an icon strip, opening over the content. |
| `LeftMinimal` | Always Minimal: no pane until the toggle button opens one over the content. |

### NavigationShellDisplayMode

```cpp
enum class NavigationShellDisplayMode
```

What a [NavigationShell](#uinavigationshell)'s pane is doing right now.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Minimal` | No pane showing while closed. An open pane overlays the content and closes on a click outside it. |
| `Compact` | An icon strip (compact_pane_length() wide) while closed; an open pane overlays the content. |
| `Expanded` | An inline pane beside the content, shrinking to the strip when closed. |

### NavigationShellSelectionFollowsFocus

```cpp
enum class NavigationShellSelectionFollowsFocus
```

Whether a [NavigationShell](#uinavigationshell) selects the item the arrow keys land on.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Disabled` | The default: the arrow keys move a cursor, Enter/Space select. |
| `Enabled` | Whatever item the arrow keys land on is selected at once. |

### NavEntryKind

```cpp
enum class NavEntryKind
```

What a [NavEntry](#struct-naventry) is: an item, a section header or a separator.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Item` | A selectable, invokable row. |
| `Header` | A section title showing the entry's text; folded away while the pane is closed compact. |
| `Separator` | A horizontal rule between groups of items. |
